E1.text:
Thus $H_1'=H_1$. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction},
with attachments $A$ and the fixed planar graph on $A$
with edge set $E$, lists every possible $H_1$. Adjoining $H_0$ to each gives every
possible $G$, but the enumeration~\supp{E1} excludes
all resulting graphs. Hence no bridge contains such a path.

E2.text:
component cannot be drawn for either choice $(1,2,2)$
or $(2,1,1)$. An edge $s_it_j$ on $\{1,3\}$ excludes the
first choice, and one on $\{2,3\}$ excludes the second.
Retaining $\Psi_1$, $B$ and one such bridge, or one such
edge on each pair, therefore gives a nontoroidal subgraph.
By minimality, it is $G$.

Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:mohar} to $B\cup C_0$, where
$C_0=abdca$. Its auxiliary graph is three-connected by
\cite[Lemma~4.2]{Mohar1994}, applied to the $C_0$-bridge
$B$ in the three-connected graph $G+E(C_0)$. Thus outcome
(c) does not occur. Outcome (a) would give disjoint
$a$--$d$ and $b$--$c$ paths with internal vertices in
$D$, contrary to Lemma~\ref{dis:opposite-order}.
Hence $B$ contains a tripod.

Some attachment path of the tripod is nontrivial.
Otherwise removing its three attachments leaves two
disjoint trees in $D$. Join them by a shortest path
in $D$ and contract to two adjacent vertices, each
adjacent to all three attachments. Together with
$\Psi_1$, this gives a $K_5$ minor~\supp{W8}.

Since the fourth attachment has a neighbor in connected $D$,
take a path $P$ from it to a vertex of the tripod in $D$,
with internal vertices in $D$ and meeting the tripod only
at its last vertex. Contract the unused vertices of $D$
onto the tripod and $P$. Shorten the tripod as in the
proof of Lemma~\ref{endpoint:primitive}, retaining $P$
and choosing the attachment path through its last vertex
as the nontrivial one if there is such a path. Shorten
$P$ to an edge. This gives $T(g)$ on the tripod's
attachments, with the fourth attachment adjacent to
$u$, $p'$ or $q'$.

Shorten another four-attachment component in the same
way, or a three-attachment component to $T(g')$ by
Lemma~\ref{dis:exterior-triangles}. Each retained $T$
has nonplanar triangle completion, so the reduced bridges
still cannot be drawn in simple faces. The shortened
graph remains nontoroidal and hence equals $G$ by
minimality. In particular, a bridge on $s_i,t_i,v$
is $T(s_i)$ or $T(t_i)$, since $T(v)$ has a degree-three
vertex adjacent to both ends of $s_it_i$.

Up to interchanging $A_1,A_2$ and the indices $1,2$, the
fourth attachment of $B$ is $c$ and the tripod attaches
at $a,b,d$. If $g=d$, one of $p',q'$ has neighborhood
$\{a,b,u\}$, contrary to
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a). If $c$ is
adjacent to $p'$, or symmetrically $q'$, the paths
$auq'd$ and $bp'c$ for $g=a$, or $aq'd$ and
$bup'c$ for $g=b$, contradict
Lemma~\ref{dis:opposite-order}. If $c$ is adjacent to
$u$ and $g=b$, the paths $ap'd$ and $buc$ give the
same contradiction. Thus $g=a$, $u$ is adjacent to
$a,c$, and $p',q'$ are adjacent to $b,d,u$.
The only other form interchanges $A_1,A_2$, and the same
description applies to the other four-attachment
component after relabeling. Every resulting graph has
a proper minor failing all twelve choices~\supp{E2}, a contradiction.

E3.text: Put $H_0=B+ac+cd+bd$. For the simple faces following $P_1,P_2$, the graph $H_{\mathrm{simp}}$ contains $H_0$. The edge $af$ excludes $(P_1;s_2,t_2)$. For $(P_2;s_1,t_1)$, we have $H_{\mathrm{rep}}=H_0$, while $H_{\mathrm{simp}}$ consists of the cycle $abfea$ and the edge $af$, which can be drawn inside that cycle without crossings. Thus Lemma~\ref{dis:joint-test} makes $G$ toroidal exactly when $H_0$ is planar, also with any allowed minor in place of $B$. Keeping $B$, the edge $cd$ and the paths $apc,brd$, then contracting these paths to $ac,bd$, shows that $H_0$ is a minor of $G$ and has no $K_5$ minor. It is nonplanar, so it contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with attachment set $A$ and the path $acdb$ as the fixed planar graph. This gives an allowed minor $B'$ with at most nine interior vertices and $B'+ac+cd+bd$ nonplanar. Thus $(\Psi_1\cup B')+af$ is nontoroidal, so minimality gives $B'=B$. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists these forms with no required subdivision edges. Adjoining $\Psi_1$ and $af$ to each candidate gives a graph with a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E3}, a contradiction. Hence $B$ has the required disk drawing, and Lemma~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation} makes $D$ a single vertex.

E4.text:
Suppose every bridge with at least two interior vertices has
three attachments and a planar relevant completion. The
possible bridges are then those with one interior vertex and
the forms in Proposition~\ref{prop:three-root-disjoint}.
At most three four-attachment bridges have the same attachment
set, since four would give $K_{4,4}$ and hence a $K_5$ minor.
We combine these bridges with disjoint interiors, subject to
the attachment restrictions and Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}.
A bridge containing $P_m$ includes that path and all
$\Psi_1$-bridges meeting its interior, so its form also
accounts for the length of $P_m$. These enumerations are
recorded in~\supp{E4,~E5}. The next lemma says that if a bridge with three attachments,
together with four vertices having those attachments as their
neighborhood, is toroidal, then adding some two edges between
its attachments gives a planar graph.

We now form graphs by adding these bridges
to $\Psi_1$ with disjoint interiors, using
at most three on any one triple by
Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}, and at most five
in total. By Lemma~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation},
there is at most one four-attachment vertex
on each set $\{s_i,t_i,s_j,t_j\}$. We also
allow any subset of the six edges $s_it_j$
with $i\ne j$. With five three-attachment bridges, allow no
other additions.
We retain only graphs satisfying
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a)
and Lemma~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation},
and exclude disjoint $s_i$--$t_j$ and
$s_j$--$t_i$ paths through distinct bridges
by Lemma~\ref{dis:opposite-order}.
The obstruction check in~\supp{E4} leaves only $\mathfrak T_{48}$ and $\mathfrak T_{58}$, neither of which has a four-attachment bridge. Together with
$\mathfrak T_5,\mathfrak T_{68}$ and
$\mathfrak T_{69}$, these give the graphs
in the statement.

E5.text:
Suppose every bridge with at least two interior vertices has
three attachments and a planar relevant completion. The
possible bridges are then those with one interior vertex and
the forms in Proposition~\ref{prop:three-root-disjoint}.
At most three four-attachment bridges have the same attachment
set, since four would give $K_{4,4}$ and hence a $K_5$ minor.
We combine these bridges with disjoint interiors, subject to
the attachment restrictions and Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}.
A bridge containing $P_m$ includes that path and all
$\Psi_1$-bridges meeting its interior, so its form also
accounts for the length of $P_m$. These enumerations are
recorded in~\supp{E4,~E5}. The next lemma says that if a bridge with three attachments,
together with four vertices having those attachments as their
neighborhood, is toroidal, then adding some two edges between
its attachments gives a planar graph.

Exclude a graph if a degree-three interior vertex has adjacent neighbors, or if both $s_it_j$ and $s_jt_i$ occur for $i\ne j$, by Lemmas~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a) and~\ref{dis:opposite-order}. If $s_mt_m$ is absent, require a bridge with both $s_m,t_m$ among its attachments, since $P_m$ lies in such a bridge. We do not choose the paths inside the candidates or require three disjoint $s_m$--$t_m$ paths. The family therefore includes additional graphs, but every graph under consideration occurs in it. Since some $P_m$ is not an edge, \eqref{dis:shortest} gives $s_mt_m\notin E(G)$. We therefore consider candidates with at least one of these three edges absent. Among those whose bridges all have at most one interior vertex, the enumeration~\supp{E5} leaves $\mathfrak T_{32},\quad \mathfrak T_{43},\quad
\mathfrak T_{61}$. Among those with a bridge of form $T,S$ or $Q$, it leaves $\mathfrak T_{38},\quad \mathfrak T_{45},\quad
\mathfrak T_{48},\quad \mathfrak T_{66},\quad
\mathfrak T_{67}$.

No candidate with a four-cycle form remains. These checks cover all the bridge forms, with graphs containing both a $T,S,Q$ form and a four-cycle form included in both checks. Every other candidate has a torus embedding, a $K_5$ minor, a cut of order at most two or a proper nontoroidal minor, as recorded in~\supp{E5}. The same family with all three edges $s_mt_m$ present gives
$\mathfrak T_{48}$ and $\mathfrak T_{58}$, already covered by
Theorem~\ref{dis:endpoint-only}. The three checks above
therefore give the stated list.

E6.text: Suppose neither $h_b$ nor $bc$ occurs. Contract $cf$ and take a torus embedding of this proper minor. Identify the two boundary copies of $P_1$ in its incident facial disks, keeping all other boundary appearances distinct. The path $P_1$ then lies inside the resulting region apart from its ends. By the rotation table~\supp{R3}, this region is either the annulus $ac\mid bd$ or a disk with attachment sequence $a,c,b,d,c$ or $a,c,b,c,d,c$. Every $\Psi_1$-bridge inside $B$ meets the interior of $P_1$, so lies in this region. No other face contains both $a,d$, so any present $h_a$ or $ad$ lies there too. The annulus would make $H_1$ planar by Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}. The first disk would make $H_1+bc+cd$ planar by Lemma~\ref{lem:embedding-extension}, so $H_1$ would again be planar. Both contradict its nonplanarity. Thus only the last disk occurs. Joining its consecutive attachments gives the edges $ac,bc,cd$, so $(B\cup H_{\mathrm{ext}})+ac+bc+cd$ is planar. Its subgraph $H_1-bd$ is therefore planar, which means every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $H_1$, including $H_2'$, uses $bd$. If neither $h_a$ nor $ad$ occurs, contracting $ed$ instead gives $H_1-ac$ planar, so every such subdivision uses $ac$. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore lists every possible $B$ using the six choices of $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$, the added edges $ac,bd$, and the subdivision edges and planar completions required above. Adjoining $J_1\cup J_2$, the edges $cf,ed$ and the chosen $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$ to each candidate gives the graphs to be checked. The checks in~\supp{E6} leave only $\mathfrak T_{21}$ and $\mathfrak T_{63}$.

E7.text: The paths $P_x,P_y,s_xps_y,t_xrt_y$ give $B\cup C$ as a $K_5$-minor-free minor of $G$. It is nonplanar by Lemma~\ref{dis:four-cycles}, so it contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision. Every such subdivision uses $s_yt_y$, whose deletion leaves the planar graph $B\cup s_ys_xt_xt_y$. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with attachment set $A$ and $H_0=C$. Since every single allowed operation makes the completion planar, the resulting allowed minor is $B$ itself, and $B$ has at most $|A|+5=9$ interior vertices. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore lists every possible $B$, with $s_yt_y$ required in the subdivision. Up to interchanging $A_1,A_2$, only one listed form has $B\cup K_4[A]$ three-connected, no disjoint $s_x$--$t_y$ and $s_y$--$t_x$ paths, and no degree-three interior vertex with adjacent neighbors in $G$~\supp{E7}. Its interior is $\{p',q',v\}$, with $N(p')=N(q')=\{s_x,s_y,v\}$ and remaining edges $vt_x,vt_y$.

E8.text: The paths $apc,brd$ and the edge $P_x=cd$ give $H$ as a $K_5$-minor-free minor of $G$. Since $H$ is nonplanar, it contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision. Every such subdivision uses $cd$, since $H-cd=B+ac+bd$ is planar. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with attachment set $A$ and $H_0=acdb$. Every single allowed operation makes this completion planar, so the resulting allowed minor is $B$ itself, and $B$ has at most $|A|+5=9$ interior vertices. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore lists every possible $B$, with $cd$ required in the subdivision. The enumeration~\supp{E8} keeps those for which $B+ac+bd$ is planar, every single allowed operation makes $B+ac+cd+bd$ planar, $B\cup K_4[A]$ is three-connected, and neither $H$ nor the minor $\Psi_1\cup B$ with $P_w$ shortened to $ef$ has a $K_5$ minor. Nine labeled bridges remain, giving the five displayed forms up to interchanging $A_1,A_2$.

E9.text:
\begin{proposition}[Nonplanar completions with four attachments]\label{r2:nonplanar-list}
If $B$ is nonplanar and $G=B\cup\Psi_2$, then $G$ is isomorphic to one of
$\mathfrak{T}_{17},\mathfrak{T}_{18},\mathfrak{T}_{19},\mathfrak{T}_{22},\mathfrak{T}_{24},\mathfrak{T}_{26},\mathfrak{T}_{30},\mathfrak{T}_{34}, \mathfrak{T}_{39},\mathfrak{T}_{48},\mathfrak{T}_{52},\mathfrak{T}_{57},\mathfrak{T}_{66},\mathfrak{T}_{74}.$
If $(n_c,n_d)=(3,2)$, $G\cong\mathfrak{T}_{11}$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Take $E=\varnothing$ in the first case and $E=\{ab,ac,bc\}$
in the second. In either case, $B+E$ is nonplanar by
the hypothesis or Lemma~\ref{r2:32}, and is contained
in every applicable test of Lemma~\ref{r2:four-tests}.
By Lemma~\ref{r2:test-minors}, it is a $K_5$-minor-free minor
of $G$, so it contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision.
Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with attachments
$a,b,c,d$. It gives an allowed minor $B'$ with at most nine
interior vertices such that $B'+E$ still contains a
$K_{3,3}$ subdivision. The interior remains connected,
and every attachment keeps an interior neighbor.
Replacing $B$ by $B'$ therefore leaves every applicable
test nonplanar, since each contains $B'+E$. By
Lemma~\ref{r2:four-tests}, the resulting minor of $G$
is nontoroidal, so minimality gives $B'=B$. We list these forms using
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction}, with
attachments $a,b,c,d$, added edges $E$, no outside
vertices and no further interior components.
Join all interior pieces by a minimal set of interior
edges and add one interior neighbor at each attachment
that has none, considering every permitted choice.
The reduction above shows that this list contains $B$.
Adjoin two vertices with each of the neighborhoods
$\{a,b,c\}$ and $\{a,b,d\}$ in the first case, and three
and two, respectively, in the second. The records in~\supp{E9} leave exactly the stated graphs.
Every other graph is excluded by five branch sets of a
$K_5$ minor, a separating set of at most two vertices,
or an edge whose deletion or contraction leaves a
nontoroidal graph. These contradict, respectively,
$K_5$-minor-freeness, three-connectivity or minimality.

E10.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction},
with attachments $x,c,d$ and added edges $xc,xd$,
lists the reduced bridges before $x$ is separated.
Replace each edge $xv$ by $av$ or $bv$ and add
an edge to the interior at $a$ or $b$ if needed,
considering every possible choice. This includes
every reduction above. Adjoin three vertices
with neighborhood $\{a,b,c\}$ and two with
neighborhood $\{a,b,d\}$. The enumeration~\supp{E10} gives $2{,}953$
candidates up to isomorphisms fixing the attachments.
Of these, $2{,}159$ have a $K_5$ minor, $92$ have
a separating set of at most two vertices, and $702$
have a proper nontoroidal minor. These exclude
every candidate, so $H$ cannot be planar.

E11.text: Before combining the forms, remove any having a proper minor that preserves its neighborhood and the required connectivity, and preserves which of the four completions are planar for $D_c,D_d$ or keeps $H_1+ac+ad$ nonplanar for $D_1$. Such a reduction would give a proper allowed minor of $B$ keeping all four tests nonplanar. For separate components $D_c,D_d$, combine their retained forms with each of the eleven forms of $B_0$ and each permitted subset of $\{aw,bw\}$, or with the two single vertices. For one component $D_1$, combine its retained form with those two vertices. The reductions above show that $G$ occurs among these combinations. The records in~\supp{E11} give $33$ remaining forms for $D_c$, $54$ for $D_1$, and all their combinations. Keeping those with $B$ planar leaves $1{,}471$ candidates. The checks leave exactly three obstructions, $\mathfrak T_{56},\mathfrak T_{72},\mathfrak T_{73}$, all with one component $D_0$.

E12.text: The tree is therefore a star with center adjacent to $b,c,d$, or a path $g_1m_1g_2m_2g_3$, where $\{g_1,g_2,g_3\}=\{b,c,d\}$. For the star, its center is adjacent to both $u,v$, or to one while a vertex of $\{b,c,d\}$ is adjacent to the other. For the path, $m_1,m_2$ are adjacent to different vertices of $\{u,v\}$, or both are adjacent to one while a vertex of $\{b,c,d\}$ is adjacent to the other. The $31$ forms in~\supp{E12} leave exactly $\mathfrak T_{40},\mathfrak T_{53},\mathfrak T_{56},\mathfrak T_{73}$.

E13.text: Suppose $b,c,d$ lie in three components $D_b,D_c,D_d$. For each $g\in\{b,c,d\}$, Lemma~\ref{r2:a-cut-single} leaves $D_g=\{g\}$, two single vertices in $D_g-g$, or one of the nine forms for $B_g$. Combine these for $g=b,c,d$, with each choice of $\{s,t\}$ among $\{a,u\},\{a,v\},\{u,v\}$ and every permitted set of original edges $gs,gt$ other than $ag$. When $D_g=\{g\}$, join $g$ to $u$, $v$ or both. In~\supp{E13}, the combinations are checked using subgraph containment. A DRAT proof certifies that every allowed combination is a subgraph of a recorded toroidal graph or contains a recorded nontoroidal graph. A subgraph of a toroidal graph is toroidal, and minimality makes $G$ equal to any nontoroidal subgraph it contains. Thus $G$ is one of the recorded nontoroidal graphs. The checks leave only $\mathfrak T_{51},\mathfrak T_{72}$, and in neither does any $D_g-g$ consist of two single vertices.

E14.text: The combinations in~\supp{E14} include both partitions of $b,c,d$ in the table, up to interchanging $c,d$, and all permitted original edges. As in Proposition~\ref{r2:ab-cut-outcome}, before combining we discard any form with a proper minor preserving its neighborhood, the stated connectivity conditions and which completions in the table are planar. All $1{,}229$ resulting candidates are excluded by the recorded checks. Thus the two-component case gives no obstruction, and the one-component and three-component cases give the stated list.

E15.text: The triangle completion of $B_b$ is three-connected by Lemma~\ref{lem:triangle-completion}, since $D_b-b$ is a component of $G-\{b,c,w\}$. It is a minor of $G$, using the internally disjoint paths $bpc$, $bqap'w$ and $cq'w$ for $bc,bw,cw$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. While $D_b$ keeps its neighbors at $c,w$, the four tests depend on $B_b$ only through $B_b+cw+bw$ and $B_b+cw+bc$. Replacing $B_b$ by a proper allowed minor gives an allowed minor of $B$, since its interior stays adjacent to $w$, the vertices $a,c$ keep $p',q'$, and $d$ keeps $w$. By minimality, no such minor keeps both completions nonplanar. Lemma~\ref{core:two-cap-critical}, with $c,w,b$ as $x,y,z$, therefore makes $B_b$ either $Q(b;c,w)$ or one of the two four-cycle forms. The enumeration~\supp{E15} applies Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} after identifying $c,w$ to a vertex $x$, with attachments $b,x$ and added edge $bx$. It then splits $x$ back into $c,w$, assigning each original edge at $x$ to one of them and adding an edge to an interior vertex at whichever has no interior neighbor. With $\Psi_2$, $p',q'$ and $dw$, the three forms above are among its $24$ candidates. Each has a separating set of at most two vertices or a proper nontoroidal minor.

E16.text: Choose one of these nonplanar completions. Its bridge has connected interior, since Lemma~\ref{r2:one-attachment}(ii) would otherwise give two single vertices whose triangle completion is planar. Retain a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of the chosen completion. Since $B_b+cw$ and $B_d+aw$ are planar, the subdivision uses $bc$ or $ad$, respectively. Reduce the chosen bridge while retaining the subdivision, its connected interior and an interior neighbor at each attachment. In the other bridge, keep one interior component, delete the others and contract the retained component to one vertex. Its neighborhood is the full attachment triple by Lemma~\ref{r2:one-attachment}(ii). Both bridges keep their attachment sets, and their interiors remain connected through $w$, so this gives an allowed minor of $B$. The chosen completion stays nonplanar, and in the other three tests the bridge containing $D_b$ is still adjacent to all of $X$. Thus all four tests remain nonplanar, so minimality leaves $B$ unchanged. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists every possible $B_b$ with attachments $b,c,w$, added edges $cw,bc$ and required edge $bc$, or every possible $B_d$ with attachments $d,a,w$, added edges $aw,ad$ and required edge $ad$. An original edge $bw$ or $dw$ may lie on the retained subdivision, so that segment is taken both as an edge and as a path with one interior vertex. The records in~\supp{E16} include both choices of the nonplanar completion. Each of the $156$ candidates has nonplanar $B$, a $K_5$ minor, a separating set of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor, a contradiction.

E17.text: Retain a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $B_1+bd+cw$. It uses $bd$, since deleting this edge leaves the planar graph $B_1+cw$. The vertices of this subdivision outside $\{b,c,d,w\}$ may lie in different components of $B_1-\{b,c,d,w\}$. By \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}, every such component has a neighbor at $w$ and at $b$ or $d$. Retain a $b$--$d$ path in $D_1$ and a neighbor of $c$ outside $\{b,c,d,w\}$. Since $D_1$ avoids $c,w$, the internal vertices of the path lie in one component of $B_1-\{b,c,d,w\}$. The chosen neighbor of $c$ lies in one such component as well. Thus at most two further components are needed. By Lemma~\ref{r2:retained-components}, contract each to one vertex and keep a minimal set of attaching edges satisfying \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}. The retained subdivision keeps $B+ac+bd$ nonplanar. In the other three tests, the bridge containing $D_1$ is still adjacent to all of $X$. The conditions in \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity} keep the interior of $B$ connected and give every attachment an interior neighbor. Thus the reduction is allowed and keeps all four tests nonplanar, so minimality leaves $B$ unchanged. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists every possible $B_1$, with attachments $b,c,d,w$, added edges $bd,cw$, the original edges $bw,dw$ permitted on the subdivision, the requirements \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}, and at most two further interior components. Adding $a$ and the three pairs of twins gives the $5{,}819$ candidates in~\supp{E17}. Each has nonplanar $B$, a $K_5$ minor, a separating set of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor.

E18.text:
Now suppose all triangle completions are planar.
Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement} makes every component
a singleton. The graph is determined by the numbers
of vertices with neighborhoods
$\{a,b,c\},\{a,b,d\},\{a,c,d\},\{b,c,d\}$,
and whether $cd$ is present. At least two vertices have
each of the first two neighborhoods, and there are at
most nine in total. These give the $252$ choices checked
in~\supp{E18}, leaving only
$\mathfrak T_9,\mathfrak T_{10},\mathfrak T_{16}$,
all without $cd$
(Figure~\ref{fig:psi2-singleton-obstructions}).
Every other graph has a cut of at most two vertices,
is toroidal, or has a proper nontoroidal minor.

E19.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists
these forms using $E=\varnothing$ or $E=\{xy\}$,
over all choices of $x,y$. Retain the forms whose
three two-edge completions are nonplanar and combine
each with $\Psi_2$ and $v$. There are two choices for
the attachment triple of $B$ and three other triples
for $N(v)$, giving the $5{,}934$ graphs in~\supp{E19}.
Each has a cut of at most two vertices, a $K_5$ minor,
or a proper nontoroidal minor, contradicting a defining
property of $G$.

E20.text: By Lemmas~\ref{r2:component-count} and~\ref{r2:eight-bridge-forms}, $G$ consists of $\Psi_2$, one to four bridges of the eight listed forms, and possibly $cd$, with at least one bridge having more than one interior vertex. Assigning each form's attachments to three of $a,b,c,d$ in every possible order gives $76$ labeled bridges up to isomorphisms fixing the attachments. Combining these with disjoint interiors under the preceding conditions, allowing repetitions and including or omitting $cd$, gives $3{,}163{,}020$ combinations. We discard combinations with two disjoint twin triples, three distinct twin triples containing the same two vertices, or a bridge with four attachments for some choice of the four twins. These exclusions remain valid when further bridges or $cd$ are added, since only $a,b,c,d$ gain neighbors and none is a degree-three vertex with a twin. Indeed, $a,b$ have degree at least four, while a twin of $c$ would have to be $a$ or $b$ to be adjacent to both $p,q$, and the same argument applies to $d$. Thus existing degree-three twins keep their neighborhoods. If adding $cd$ puts an edge inside one of these neighborhoods, Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a) excludes the graph, and otherwise the twin triples remain. A component with four attachments also retains those attachments when it becomes part of a larger component. We further discard any combination containing a smaller nontoroidal combination, since it has a proper nontoroidal minor. After these exclusions, the checks in~\supp{E20} give a cut of at most two vertices, a torus embedding, or a proper nontoroidal minor for every combination except four. These four graphs are all isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{15}$.

E21.text:
Thus $B'$ has nonplanar triangle completion. Contracting
$\operatorname{Int}(B)$ keeps $H$ nonplanar, so the same criterion
and minimality make $\operatorname{Int}(B)$ a single vertex.
A $b$--$d$ path with interior in $\operatorname{Int}(B)$ shows
that the triangle completion of $B'$ is a minor of $H$, so it
contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision.
An allowed reduction of $B'$ keeping this subdivision keeps $H$
nonplanar and would again give a proper nontoroidal minor.
Thus Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} and
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction}, with attachments
$a,b,d$ and the added triangle, give every possible $B'$.
The $216$ forms, with $bd$ absent or present, give $432$ graphs.
Each has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, or a proper
nontoroidal minor~\supp{E21}.

E22.text: The nonplanar graph $H$ has no $K_5$ minor, so it contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision. If $bd$ is present, Corollary~\ref{r1:five-criterion} applied to the toroidal graph $G-bd$ makes $H-bd$ planar, so every such subdivision uses $bd$. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with the five attachments and the fixed planar graph on them consisting of $ab,ac,ad,ae$, together with $bd$ when present. The reduction preserves the connected interior, all five attachments and the nonplanarity of the completion, so the resulting minor is nontoroidal by Corollary~\ref{r1:five-criterion}. Minimality forces the reduction to be trivial. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} gives $217{,}376$ candidates. All except $\mathfrak T_{20},\mathfrak T_{23}$ have a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices, a proper nontoroidal minor, or two twin triples meeting in zero or two vertices~\supp{E22}.

E23.text:
The graph $B'+ab+ac+ad+ae+bc+de$ is still a minor
of $G$, so Lemma~\ref{r1:matching-test} makes
$B'+ab+ac+ad+ae$ nonplanar. Thus $\Psi_3\cup B'$
fails both tests of Lemma~\ref{r1:missing-a-criterion}.
Minimality forces $B'=B$ and $G=\Psi_3\cup B$.
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction}
therefore includes $B$ among $26{,}633$ forms.
Every resulting graph other than $\mathfrak T_{54}$
is toroidal or has a $K_5$ minor or a proper
nontoroidal minor~\supp{E23}, so
$G\cong\mathfrak T_{54}$.

E24.text:
The resulting nontoroidal minor cannot equal $G$, since $\{a,b,d\}$
meets $\{a,b,c\}$ twice.

With two other bridges, Lemma~\ref{core:assembly-general}(ii)
gives one with nonplanar triangle completion. Contracting the
other to a vertex keeps $H_4$ nonplanar, since its $b$--$d$ path
supplies the missing triangle edge. Minimality fixes that vertex.
For one bridge, keep $H_1+ab+ad$ nonplanar. For two, keep the
nonplanar triangle completion of the uncontracted bridge.
In each case both embedding tests still fail, so
Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} and
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} give every
possibility: $349$ forms in the first case and $216$ in the
second. Every resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at
most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E24}.

E25.text:
nonplanar triangle completion $H_1+ab+ad+bd$.
Since $H_3$ contains $H_2+bd$, Lemma~\ref{r1:missing-a-cut} gives
twins $p',q'$ with neighborhood $\{c,e,w\}$.
Contract the rest of $\operatorname{Int}(B)$ to $w$, retaining
only $bw,dw$ and the six edges at $p',q'$ in $B$.
The disk test and the annular choice $E_0=\{bd\}$ still fail
because they contain $H_1+ab+ad+bd$.
For $E_0=\varnothing$, the graph $H_2+bd$ has a $K_{3,3}$ minor:
the sets $\{p'\},\{q'\},\{b,d\}$ are each adjacent to $c,e,w$.
Thus minimality fixes this reduced $B$.
Keeping the triangle completion of $H_1$ nonplanar preserves
the same failures, so Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision}
and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} give $216$
forms. Each resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most
two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E25}.

E26.text:
with $\Psi_3$, deleting every other bridge and cross edge.
Contract the component with neighborhood $\{a,c,e\}$ to $v$ and
$\operatorname{Int}(B)$ to $w$, keeping
$N(v)=\{a,c,e\}$ and $N(w)=\{b,c,d,e\}$.
In the retained graph, $H$ contains that triangle completion as a minor,
using $ab,ad$ and the path $bwd$.
The annular condition fails because the other bridges have
two different attachment triples. Minimality therefore makes
$G$ this retained graph. Keeping the triangle completion
nonplanar preserves both failures, so
Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} and
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} give $216$ forms.
The case of a bridge with attachments $\{a,c,e\}$ is symmetric.
All $432$ graphs have a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two
vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E26}.

E27.text:
For $\{a,d,e\}$, contract $\Psi_3$ to triangles.
For $\{a,c,d\}$, also contract $\operatorname{Int}(B)$ into $d$.
For $\{a,b,d\}$, additionally contract $c$ into $d$.

Suppose such a bridge $B_1$ has nonplanar triangle completion
but a planar two-edge completion. Halin's theorem and
Lemma~\ref{core:three-root-cut} give twins in $G$ and an
allowed minor of one of the forms $T,S,Q$.
The twins' neighborhood must meet each of $\{a,b,c\},\{a,d,e\}$ once.
For the three possible attachment triples, this leaves nine forms.
Contract $\operatorname{Int}(B)$ to $w$. If $B_1$ does not attach
at both $b,d$, the outside path avoids its interior and can be
contracted to $bd$. Retain only this exterior and the allowed
minor of $B_1$. Eight of the nine resulting graphs have a proper
nontoroidal minor~\supp{E27}.

E28.text:
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} gives
$349$ possibilities for $B_1$. Every resulting graph
has a $K_5$ minor, a cut of at most two vertices,
or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E28}.
Thus every other bridge with nonempty interior
has planar triangle completion, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:flat-replacement} makes its interior
a single vertex.

E29.text:
Suppose $n_e=3$. The applicable row gives a single
nonplanar completion $B+E'$.
Contracting $J_1,J_2$ to triangles and $bd$ into $d$,
then deleting unused vertices, gives the minor
$B+ac+ad+ae+cd+de$ of $G$.
Hence $B+E'$ has no $K_5$ minor.
Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} to a
$K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it, with attachments
$a,c,d,e$ and added edges $E'$.
The reduction preserves the connected interior, all four attachments and the nonplanarity of the completion by $E'$. Thus the resulting minor is nontoroidal, so minimality forces the reduction to leave $B$ unchanged.
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} gives
$9{,}127$ possibilities without $cd$ and $8{,}967$
with $cd$. Every resulting graph has a proper
nontoroidal minor obtained by deleting or
contracting one edge~\supp{E29}, a contradiction.
Thus $n_e=2$, and the first two rows give the
claimed form of $G$ and its two nonplanar completions.

E30.text: Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction}, using $E'$ and requiring $de$ when $H_0$ is planar, therefore includes every possibility. The two choices of $E$ and the two cases for $H_0$ give $66{,}384$ candidates. Every resulting graph is toroidal, has a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor, or is isomorphic to one of thirteen graphs $\mathfrak T_i$~\supp{E30}. Nine have twin triples meeting in zero or two vertices, leaving $\mathfrak T_{14},\mathfrak T_{37},\mathfrak T_{41},\mathfrak T_{59}$.

E31.text: The graph $(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce$ is toroidal exactly when $B+bc$ is planar. If a closed regular neighborhood of $\Psi_3+ce$ in a torus embedding has genus one, its facial walks containing $b,c,d$ have sequences $bcd,bcdc$~\supp{R9}, and both corresponding tests contain $B+bc$. If the neighborhood has genus zero, no boundary walk contains all three attachments, and the only possible annuli meeting all three have sequences $bc\mid ad$ or $bc\mid de$. Their tests are $B+bc+ad$ and $B+bc+de$, each equivalent to planarity of $B+bc$ because the added vertex $a$ or $e$ has degree one. Conversely, choose a plane embedding of $\Psi_3+ce$ with the two facial walks containing $b,c$ and $a,d$ recorded in~\supp{R9}. Remove an open disk from each of these faces and join the two new boundary circles by a cylinder. This gives a torus embedding with an annular face whose attachment sequences are $bc\mid ad$. If $B+bc$ is planar, so is $B+bc+ad$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} places $B$ in this annulus. Contract a $c$--$e$ path whose interior avoids $\Psi_3\cup B$ to $ce$ and keep only $\Psi_3\cup B\cup ce$. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} to a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $B+bc$. The reduction preserves the attachments, connected interior and nonplanarity of $B+bc$, so the resulting minor remains nontoroidal. Minimality and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore give the $563$ forms with added edge $bc$. Every resulting graph has a proper nontoroidal minor except one copy of $\mathfrak T_{41}$, for which $B+bd+cd$ is planar~\supp{E31}, a contradiction. Exchanging $b,e$ and $c,d$ handles $\{c,d,e\}$.

E32.text: It remains to consider $\{a,b,d\}$ and $\{a,c,e\}$, which the same symmetry interchanges. Suppose $B$ has attachments $\{a,b,d\}$. If another bridge has attachments $\{a,b,c\}$, $\{a,d,e\}$, $\{a,c,d\}$ or $\{c,d,e\}$, contract its interior to $v$. In the first three cases, also contract an outside $c$--$e$ path to $ce$. Keep only $B$ and $\Psi_3+ce+v$, or $\Psi_3+v$ in the last case. The graphs $\Psi_3+ce+v$ and $\Psi_3+v$ in the respective cases are nonplanar. In their torus embeddings, the facial walks containing $a,b,d$ have sequence $abad$, with $abd$ also possible when $N(v)=\{a,c,d\}$~\supp{R10}. Every complementary region is therefore a disk, and Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} requires $B+ab+ad$ to be planar. Retaining a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in this nonplanar completion keeps the resulting minor nontoroidal. Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision}, minimality and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore give the $349$ forms with added edges $ab,ad$. Every resulting graph has a proper nontoroidal minor except two in the $\{c,d,e\}$ case, both with $B+ad+bd$ planar~\supp{E32}, again a contradiction.

E33.text:
If another bridge has attachments $\{b,c,d\}$, contract its interior to $v$ and an outside $c$--$e$ path to $ce$. If $cd$ is an edge, use $ce,cd$ instead. Keeping these additions and $\Psi_3\cup B$ gives
\[
H_0=(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce+v\quad\hbox{or}\quad H_0=(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce+cd.
\]
In both cases, $H_0-\operatorname{Int}(B)$ contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision with parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,c\}$, using $cpa$, either $cd$ or $cvd$, the edge $ce$, and the edges at $r,z$. Every complementary region is therefore a disk. The facial walks containing $a,b,d$ give exactly $abad,abd,adbd$~\supp{R11}. The first and last give the tests $B+ab+ad$ and $B+ad+bd$, while $abd$ gives the triangle completion, whose planarity implies both. Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{r1:two-cap-test}
H_0\text{ is toroidal}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
B+ab+ad\text{ is planar or }B+ad+bd\text{ is planar}.
\end{equation}
Both $B+ab+ad$ and $B+ad+bd$ are nonplanar, so minimality gives $G=H_0$. If $B+ad$ is nonplanar, apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} to a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it. Both completions contain $B+ad$, so both remain nonplanar after this reduction. Minimality and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} give the $563$ forms with added edge $ad$. Every resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor except four in the $cd$ case, isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{52},\mathfrak T_{57},\mathfrak T_{58},\mathfrak T_{59}$. The first three have twin triples meeting in zero or two vertices, and the last has a choice of twins giving a component with four neighbors~\supp{E33}. Thus $B+ad$ is planar. Any proper allowed minor keeping both completions in~\eqref{r1:two-cap-test} nonplanar would contradict minimality, so Lemma~\ref{core:two-cap-critical} applies with $(x,y,z)=(a,d,b)$. Since $B+ab+bd$ is nonplanar, the $Q$ form is excluded. Hence $B$ consists of the cycle $up'u'q'u$, the edges $bu,bu'$, and either
\[
N_B(d)=\{p',q'\},\quad N_B(a)=\{u'\},
\qquad\hbox{or}\qquad
N_B(a)=\{p',q'\},\quad N_B(d)=\{u'\}.
\]
In the first case, the twin triple $\{d,u,u'\}$ is disjoint from $\{a,b,c\}$. In the second, choose the twins with neighborhood $\{a,u,u'\}$ together with $r,z$. The component outside the new $\Psi_3$ containing $b,c,p,q$ has neighbors at $u,u'$ through $b$, at $e$ through $ce$, at $d$ through $cd$ or $v$, and at $a$ through $p$. The first case contradicts the assumption that distinct twin triples meet in exactly one vertex. The second gives a component with five neighbors, although every component outside every choice of $\Psi_3$ has exactly three.

R1.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{dis:faces}
Every torus embedding of $\Psi_1$ is cellular with five faces.
For some $k\in\{1,2,3\}$, write
$\{i,j\}=\{1,2,3\}\setminus\{k\}$.
Omitting the twins from the boundary walks, these faces are
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item two faces, each following
$s_iP_it_i,t_jP_j^{-1}s_j$ and meeting no other path.
\item one face following
$s_kP_kt_k,t_y,t_kP_k^{-1}s_k,s_x$, where
$x,y\in\{i,j\}$ may be equal.
\item two other faces meeting the paths exactly at
$\{s_k,s_{x'}\}$ and $\{t_k,t_{y'}\}$, respectively,
where $\{x,x'\}=\{y,y'\}=\{i,j\}$.
\end{enumerate}
All twelve choices of $k$, $x$ and $y$ occur.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The graph $\Psi_1$ is connected and nonplanar, as $\Psi_1-z$ is a subdivision of
$K_{3,3}$ with parts $A_1$ and $\{p,q,r\}$, so its torus embeddings are
cellular by Youngs's theorem. Subdividing an edge does not change the faces,
so we may take each $P_i$ to be an edge. Up to automorphisms of $\Psi_1$,
there are exactly two torus embeddings~\supp{R1}. Their boundary walks,
after permuting the indices, give (i)--(iii), with $x=y$ in one and
$x\ne y$ in the other. Permuting the indices of both triples
simultaneously is an automorphism of $\Psi_1$, so the first gives the six
choices with $x=y$ and the second the six with $x\ne y$.

R2.text: Suppose (a) holds, and let $B$ be the unique $\Psi_1$-bridge. Its interior lies in one facial disk $F$. The rotation table~\supp{R2} records the cyclic sequences of attachment appearances, including repeated appearances, around every face containing all four attachments, as $F$ does. Up to cyclic shift and reversal, each sequence also occurs around a face in a torus embedding of $\Psi_1$, except $a,b,c,d$. For each of the other sequences, the Jordan--Schoenflies theorem lets us transfer the drawing of $B$ to that face and obtain a torus embedding of $H$.

In (b), the attachments are $a,b,c$. Read the facial boundary walks in~\supp{R2} for $\Psi_1/s_3t_3$ and $\Psi_1$, recording only appearances of $a,b,c$. Every such sequence containing $a,b,c$ for the contracted graph also occurs for $\Psi_1$. In particular, the order $a,b,c$ occurs in the simple face with order $a,b,d,c$ by leaving $d$ unused. Transferring the drawing of the bridge to the corresponding face therefore gives a torus embedding of $H$.

In the annular case, the boundary attachment sequences are $a,c\mid b$, $a,c\mid b,d$, $a\mid b$ or $a\mid b,d$. Each also occurs for $\Psi_1$ by~\supp{R2}, so Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} lets us insert $H_0$ and obtain a torus embedding of $H$. In the disk case, the sequences are $a,b$, $a,b,c$, $a,b,d$, $a,b,c,d$ or $a,c,d,b,d,c$. For $\Psi_1$, take the disk drawings of its two simple faces and identify only their boundary copies of $P_1$. The resulting disk has the last sequence. It also gives $a,b,c$ and $a,b,d$ by using the appearances after $b$, so only $a,b,c,d$ with all four attachments remains. Put $D=H_0-\{a,b,c,d\}$. The internal vertices of $P_1$ connect all the bridge interiors, so $D$ is connected. Every edge of $H_0$ has an end in $D$, and every attachment has a neighbor there. As in (a), Lemma~\ref{dis:four-disk-order} gives a drawing in order $a,b,d,c$, or disjoint $a$--$d$ and $b$--$c$ paths through $D$. Joining these through $D$ gives the same $K_5$ minor as in (a), with the joining path supplying $ab$. Hence the drawing in order $a,b,d,c$ exists. Using the appearances of $d,c$ after $b$ in the disk above gives a torus embedding of $H$.

R3.text: Suppose neither $h_b$ nor $bc$ occurs. Contract $cf$ and take a torus embedding of this proper minor. Identify the two boundary copies of $P_1$ in its incident facial disks, keeping all other boundary appearances distinct. The path $P_1$ then lies inside the resulting region apart from its ends. By the rotation table~\supp{R3}, this region is either the annulus $ac\mid bd$ or a disk with attachment sequence $a,c,b,d,c$ or $a,c,b,c,d,c$. Every $\Psi_1$-bridge inside $B$ meets the interior of $P_1$, so lies in this region. No other face contains both $a,d$, so any present $h_a$ or $ad$ lies there too. The annulus would make $H_1$ planar by Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}. The first disk would make $H_1+bc+cd$ planar by Lemma~\ref{lem:embedding-extension}, so $H_1$ would again be planar. Both contradict its nonplanarity. Thus only the last disk occurs. Joining its consecutive attachments gives the edges $ac,bc,cd$, so $(B\cup H_{\mathrm{ext}})+ac+bc+cd$ is planar. Its subgraph $H_1-bd$ is therefore planar, which means every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $H_1$, including $H_2'$, uses $bd$. If neither $h_a$ nor $ad$ occurs, contracting $ed$ instead gives $H_1-ac$ planar, so every such subdivision uses $ac$. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore lists every possible $B$ using the six choices of $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$, the added edges $ac,bd$, and the subdivision edges and planar completions required above. Adjoining $J_1\cup J_2$, the edges $cf,ed$ and the chosen $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$ to each candidate gives the graphs to be checked. The checks in~\supp{E6} leave only $\mathfrak T_{21}$ and $\mathfrak T_{63}$.

R4.text:
Suppose $G$ has a torus embedding and restrict it to $K$.
The connected interior of $B$ lies in one face $F$, whose
boundary contains all four attachments. For each of the
three pairs $(n_c,n_d)$, the rotations of $K$ and their
boundary attachment sequences are given in~\supp{R4}.
Let $\mathcal N$ be a closed regular neighborhood of $K$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}, if $\mathcal N$ has
genus one, every complementary region is a disk.
If it has genus zero, the complementary regions are disks
together with exactly one annulus or one torus with an
open disk removed. For a disk face, let $H_0$ consist of
the attachments and the edges joining consecutive
attachments on its boundary, as in the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}.

\begin{lemma}\label{r2:two-edge-exists}
The attachments of every $\Psi_2$-bridge $B$ with nonempty
interior can be labeled $x,y,z$ so that $B+xy+xz$ is planar.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Suppose every two-edge completion of a bridge $B$ is
nonplanar. If its attachments are $\{a,b,c\}$ or
$\{a,b,d\}$, three-connectivity gives a $c$--$d$ path
in $G-\{a,b\}$. It avoids the interior of $B$, which
has only one remaining attachment, and avoids the
chosen twins internally, since they have degree one
in this graph. Contract the path into its end belonging
to $B$, delete any new edges to $a,b$, and retain only
$B$ and $p,q,r,z$. This proper minor consists of $B$
and four twins with its attachment triple as their
neighborhood. Lemma~\ref{lem:four-twins} makes it
nontoroidal, a contradiction. Thus $B$ has attachments $\{a,c,d\}$ or $\{b,c,d\}$.
Some other component has a different attachment triple.
Otherwise $b$ or $a$ has degree four, contrary to
Lemma~\ref{r2:degree-four}. Retain $\Psi_2$, $B$, and
one such component contracted to a vertex $v$.
The attachments of $B$ and the neighbors of $v$ include all four vertices $a,b,c,d$. Suppose the graph consisting of $\Psi_2$, $B$ and the three edges at $v$ has a torus embedding. Since $B$ joins $c,d$, Lemma~\ref{r2:cellular-center} excludes an embedding in which a closed regular neighborhood of $\Psi_2$ has genus one. That neighborhood therefore has genus zero, and each boundary walk contains at most two attachment labels~\supp{R4}. Both $B$ and the three edges at $v$ have three attachments, so each must lie in a region with at least two boundary components. Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement} therefore places both in the same annulus. Since they meet all four attachments, its boundary sequences are $ac\mid bd$ or $ad\mid bc$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}, adding $ac,bd$ or $ad,bc$, respectively, would give a planar graph consisting of $B$, the three edges at $v$ and the two added edges. The edges at $v$ and the added pair connect all four vertices $a,b,c,d$ outside the interior of $B$. Choose a tree in this graph joining the three attachments of $B$, and delete the other edges outside $B$. Contract edges of the tree with an end outside the attachment set until only the three attachments remain, keeping them distinct. The two remaining edges give a planar two-edge completion of $B$, contradicting the assumption that all three such completions are nonplanar. The same argument applies after any allowed reduction
of $B$ for which all three two-edge completions remain nonplanar. Minimality
therefore makes $G$ equal to the retained graph and
forbids any such proper reduction.

Suppose a shortening in (i) or (ii) of
Lemma~\ref{r2:cycle-restoration} is
possible. It keeps the interior connected
and preserves all three attachments,
giving a proper minor of $G$.
Take a torus embedding of this minor.
The subgraph $\Psi_2$ and every bridge's
attachments are unchanged, so the disk
and annulus tests still apply. For a disk containing the shortened
bridge, take $H=C_F$, the boundary
cycle in its planar test graph.
For an annulus, a closed regular neighborhood
of $\Psi_2$ has genus zero by
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}, so no
boundary walk contains three attachments
or both $c,d$~\supp{R4}. Every bridge with
three attachments, and $cd$ if present,
therefore lies in the annulus. These
additions still meet all four vertices,
so its boundary sequences are $ac\mid bd$
or $ad\mid bc$.
Take $H$ to consist of the two added
edges of the annulus test together
with $cd$ or another bridge.
The edge $cd$ joins the two added
edges, and any bridge with three
attachments meets both. Thus $H$
is connected, contains all four
attachment appearances, and avoids
the interior of the shortened bridge. Lemma~\ref{r2:cycle-restoration}
therefore restores $B$ in the planar
test graph, keeping the other edges
and their attachment appearances fixed.
Lemma~\ref{lem:embedding-extension}
or Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}
then gives a torus embedding of $G$,
a contradiction.

R5.text:
Record only $a,c,d$ on the boundary walks of $F$.
If consecutive appearances are equal, move their incident
edges to one appearance along the intervening boundary arc,
preserving their order. Since $B_1$ meets both $c,d$,
the rotation table~\supp{R5} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement} leave only the disk sequences
$acd,acad,acacd$ and the annular pairs $ad\mid ac,ad\mid c$. We show that $B_1$ can be drawn in an annulus with $a_1,d$
on one boundary and $a_2,c$ on the other, allowing the edges
at $a$ to use $a_1$ or $a_2$. The annular cases already give
this, with $a_2$ unused for $ad\mid c$. In a disk case,
separate the appearances and use the boundary order
$a_1,c_1,a_2,c_2,d$, leaving positions unused where needed.
Draw $c_1c_2,c_1a_2,a_1d$ outside the disk without crossings,
then contract $c_1c_2$ to recover $c$. The resulting graph
is planar, with $a_1,a_2$ distinct and $a_1d,a_2c$ added.
Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} gives the required drawing.

R6.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{r1:exterior-faces}
In a torus embedding of $\Psi_3$, let $\mathcal N$ be a closed regular
neighborhood of $\Psi_3$. If $\mathcal N$ has genus one and a face meets
$b,c,d,e$, that face is a disk with attachment sequence
$a,b,a,d,a,c,a,e$, up to cyclic shift and reversal, and the other
two faces have attachment sequences $bc,de$. If $\mathcal N$ has genus zero, any face
meeting $b,c,d,e$ is an annulus with attachment sequences $bc\mid de$, and
the other three faces are disks with attachment sequences $axay$, $ax'$ and
$ay'$, where $\{x,x'\}=\{b,c\}$ and $\{y,y'\}=\{d,e\}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
$\Psi_3$ has $96$ rotation systems. Their facial walks are recorded in~\supp{R6}. No rotation system of genus zero has a face containing all four of $b,c,d,e$ in its boundary walk. The only pair of facial walks in any rotation system of genus zero whose union contains all four has attachment sequences $bc,de$. Thus, by Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}, a face meeting all four in a torus embedding with this rotation must be an annulus with attachment sequences $bc\mid de$. The other three facial walks of such a rotation have attachment sequences $axay$, $ax'$ and $ay'$, and bound disks by the same lemma. Of the genus-one rotations, the only facial attachment sequence containing all four is $abadacae$, up to cyclic shift and reversal. The other two faces have attachment sequences $bc,de$.

R7.text:
Suppose $B_1+ab+ad$ is planar. Halin's theorem and
Lemma~\ref{core:three-root-cut} give twins $p',q'$
whose neighborhood $X$ contains $a$. Since $X$ meets
each of $\{a,b,c\},\{a,d,e\}$ exactly once, it has
the form $\{a,u,v\}$ with
$u,v\in\operatorname{Int}(B_1)$. The same lemma gives
disjoint $b$--$u$ and $d$--$v$ paths.
Choose $p',q',r,z$ as the four twins.
The set $\operatorname{Int}(B)\cup\{b,c,p,q\}$ is
connected because $c$ has a neighbor in the interior of $B$
and $p,q$ join $b$ to $c$. It lies in a component
outside the new $\Psi_3$, with neighbors at $a,d,e$
through $B$ and at $u$ through the $b$--$u$ path.
Since five neighbors are excluded, this component
has exactly four neighbors and at least
$|\operatorname{Int}(B)|+4$ vertices, contrary to
the choice of $B$. Thus $B_1+ab+ad$ is nonplanar. Since $B_1+ab+ad$ has no $K_5$ minor, choose a
$K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it and apply
Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision}. This gives
an allowed minor $B_1'$ with the same three
attachments, connected interior and $B_1'+ab+ad$
nonplanar. Contract the interior of $B$ to $w$
and keep only $\Psi_3$, $B_1'$ and the edges at $w$.
The resulting minor is $\Psi_3\cup B_1'+w$, where
$N(w)=\{a,c,d,e\}$. The graph $\Psi_3+w$ contains $K_{3,3}$ with
parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,w\}$. Thus, in every torus
embedding of $\Psi_3+w$, each component of the complement
of its closed regular neighborhood is a disk by
Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}.
In every such embedding, a facial walk containing
$a,b,d$ has attachment sequence $abad$, up to
cyclic shift and reversal~\supp{R7}.
Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} therefore
requires $B_1'+ab+ad$ to be planar, a contradiction.
Hence this minor is nontoroidal, and minimality
gives $B_1'=B_1$ and $G=\Psi_3\cup B_1+w$.

R8.text:
For each of these twelve choices, the attachment sequences from
all rotations of $G-\operatorname{Int}(B)$ are recorded in~\supp{R8}.
In genus one, Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions}
gives the disk tests. In genus zero, no boundary
walk contains all four attachments, and the only
possible annulus meeting all four is $ac\mid de$, with test $B+ac+de$
by Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}.
Omitting edge sets that contain another gives the
table. Every listed test comes from a recorded
rotation, so its planarity also gives a torus embedding.

R9.text: The graph $(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce$ is toroidal exactly when $B+bc$ is planar. If a closed regular neighborhood of $\Psi_3+ce$ in a torus embedding has genus one, its facial walks containing $b,c,d$ have sequences $bcd,bcdc$~\supp{R9}, and both corresponding tests contain $B+bc$. If the neighborhood has genus zero, no boundary walk contains all three attachments, and the only possible annuli meeting all three have sequences $bc\mid ad$ or $bc\mid de$. Their tests are $B+bc+ad$ and $B+bc+de$, each equivalent to planarity of $B+bc$ because the added vertex $a$ or $e$ has degree one. Conversely, choose a plane embedding of $\Psi_3+ce$ with the two facial walks containing $b,c$ and $a,d$ recorded in~\supp{R9}. Remove an open disk from each of these faces and join the two new boundary circles by a cylinder. This gives a torus embedding with an annular face whose attachment sequences are $bc\mid ad$. If $B+bc$ is planar, so is $B+bc+ad$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} places $B$ in this annulus. Contract a $c$--$e$ path whose interior avoids $\Psi_3\cup B$ to $ce$ and keep only $\Psi_3\cup B\cup ce$. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} to a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $B+bc$. The reduction preserves the attachments, connected interior and nonplanarity of $B+bc$, so the resulting minor remains nontoroidal. Minimality and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore give the $563$ forms with added edge $bc$. Every resulting graph has a proper nontoroidal minor except one copy of $\mathfrak T_{41}$, for which $B+bd+cd$ is planar~\supp{E31}, a contradiction. Exchanging $b,e$ and $c,d$ handles $\{c,d,e\}$.

R10.text: It remains to consider $\{a,b,d\}$ and $\{a,c,e\}$, which the same symmetry interchanges. Suppose $B$ has attachments $\{a,b,d\}$. If another bridge has attachments $\{a,b,c\}$, $\{a,d,e\}$, $\{a,c,d\}$ or $\{c,d,e\}$, contract its interior to $v$. In the first three cases, also contract an outside $c$--$e$ path to $ce$. Keep only $B$ and $\Psi_3+ce+v$, or $\Psi_3+v$ in the last case. The graphs $\Psi_3+ce+v$ and $\Psi_3+v$ in the respective cases are nonplanar. In their torus embeddings, the facial walks containing $a,b,d$ have sequence $abad$, with $abd$ also possible when $N(v)=\{a,c,d\}$~\supp{R10}. Every complementary region is therefore a disk, and Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} requires $B+ab+ad$ to be planar. Retaining a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in this nonplanar completion keeps the resulting minor nontoroidal. Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision}, minimality and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore give the $349$ forms with added edges $ab,ad$. Every resulting graph has a proper nontoroidal minor except two in the $\{c,d,e\}$ case, both with $B+ad+bd$ planar~\supp{E32}, again a contradiction.

R11.text:
If another bridge has attachments $\{b,c,d\}$, contract its interior to $v$ and an outside $c$--$e$ path to $ce$. If $cd$ is an edge, use $ce,cd$ instead. Keeping these additions and $\Psi_3\cup B$ gives
\[
H_0=(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce+v\quad\hbox{or}\quad H_0=(\Psi_3\cup B)+ce+cd.
\]
In both cases, $H_0-\operatorname{Int}(B)$ contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision with parts $\{a,d,e\}$ and $\{r,z,c\}$, using $cpa$, either $cd$ or $cvd$, the edge $ce$, and the edges at $r,z$. Every complementary region is therefore a disk. The facial walks containing $a,b,d$ give exactly $abad,abd,adbd$~\supp{R11}. The first and last give the tests $B+ab+ad$ and $B+ad+bd$, while $abd$ gives the triangle completion, whose planarity implies both. Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{r1:two-cap-test}
H_0\text{ is toroidal}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
B+ab+ad\text{ is planar or }B+ad+bd\text{ is planar}.
\end{equation}
Both $B+ab+ad$ and $B+ad+bd$ are nonplanar, so minimality gives $G=H_0$. If $B+ad$ is nonplanar, apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} to a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it. Both completions contain $B+ad$, so both remain nonplanar after this reduction. Minimality and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} give the $563$ forms with added edge $ad$. Every resulting graph has a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor except four in the $cd$ case, isomorphic to $\mathfrak T_{52},\mathfrak T_{57},\mathfrak T_{58},\mathfrak T_{59}$. The first three have twin triples meeting in zero or two vertices, and the last has a choice of twins giving a component with four neighbors~\supp{E33}. Thus $B+ad$ is planar. Any proper allowed minor keeping both completions in~\eqref{r1:two-cap-test} nonplanar would contradict minimality, so Lemma~\ref{core:two-cap-critical} applies with $(x,y,z)=(a,d,b)$. Since $B+ab+bd$ is nonplanar, the $Q$ form is excluded. Hence $B$ consists of the cycle $up'u'q'u$, the edges $bu,bu'$, and either
\[
N_B(d)=\{p',q'\},\quad N_B(a)=\{u'\},
\qquad\hbox{or}\qquad
N_B(a)=\{p',q'\},\quad N_B(d)=\{u'\}.
\]
In the first case, the twin triple $\{d,u,u'\}$ is disjoint from $\{a,b,c\}$. In the second, choose the twins with neighborhood $\{a,u,u'\}$ together with $r,z$. The component outside the new $\Psi_3$ containing $b,c,p,q$ has neighbors at $u,u'$ through $b$, at $e$ through $ce$, at $d$ through $cd$ or $v$, and at $a$ through $p$. The first case contradicts the assumption that distinct twin triples meet in exactly one vertex. The second gives a component with five neighbors, although every component outside every choice of $\Psi_3$ has exactly three.
